Catching Secondary MSK Findings & Resolving Ambiguous Meniscal/Chondral Signals in < 120 ms

When reading a 144-slice 3-plane Knee MRI under high RVU volume, "satisfaction of search" causes single readers to omit 12–18% of secondary pathologies once a primary tear is dictated. Meanwhile, standard hospital AI tools operate as black-box probability bars without showing where a signal contacts the articular cortex. Creaky combines a 0.957 AUC 3-plane ensemble with deterministic computer-vision biomarkers (unmarked 1.65× high-contrast tissue zoom, subchondral cortical edge mapping, and same-plane normal reference matching).

Why We Built This Specifically for Reading Radiologists & Ortho Clinics

1. Eliminates "Satisfaction of Search" Omissions

In our audit of 2,610 clinical reports against the 3-radiologist consensus panel, single readers routinely dictated the headline injury (e.g., acute ACL rupture) but omitted secondary findings: 77.6% of true Synovitis, 44.8% of Joint Effusions, and 35.0% of subtle Meniscal Tears went unmentioned in text.

✓ Pre-populates a complete 12-structure structured checklist before sign-off

2. Cortical Containment & Articular Surface Contact

Naive CNNs hallucinate ligament tears when bright subcortical T2 bone contusions bleed across receptive fields, and confuse benign Grade II intrameniscal mucin with operative Grade III tears. We use directional cortical edge derivatives (Scharr) to verify subchondral containment and measure exact articular surface contact percentage.

✓ Always pairs AI contours with an unmarked 1.65× high-contrast tissue zoom

3. Instant Patient-Friendly Visual Handout

Patients leave orthopedic visits confused by terms like "suprapatellar recess distention" or "subchondral marrow edema." With one toggle, the workstation generates a side-by-side comparison against a healthy knee MRI from the same plane plus a plain-English summary.

✓ Zero-egress HIPAA Safe-Harbor pixel scrubber strips burned-in corner tags
